applies_why: The judge text decides the D5-vs-C5 collision by citing isolated chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23's application, and a word-count that cuts both ways, which is the verse-by-verse weighing the rule governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse.' Reading one: the judge must assess the whole pressed chain against the link's chain by their footings. Reading two: the judge may call the link underdetermined from isolated verses and word-count evidence.
why: The judge reasons from individual verses and a word-count cutting both ways, not from a chain-against-chain footing comparison, so it breaches K-C.
